title: Blackbox Protocol Manual
summary: Handle fragments and directives carefully; Blackbox progress is consequence, not just loot.

blocks.title: Overview
blocks.body: Blackbox content is meant to feel like recovered intent. Treat fragments and directives as signals with consequences, not generic collectibles.

blocks.title: First Steps
blocks.body: Read records before acting on them. Store unusual fragments, compare names in Wiki or Terminal, and avoid using directive items until you understand the route cost.

blocks.title: Core Loop
blocks.body: Find a fragment, identify its context, follow the smallest safe lead, and reassess. The best Blackbox progress is deliberate and logged.

blocks.title: Important Systems
blocks.body: Fragments, ending directives, and signal records can point at different outcomes. A quiet item may matter later, so do not discard named evidence casually.

blocks.title: Integrations
blocks.body: SignalOS, Terminal, Wiki, and TutorialCore are the natural support surfaces. Index can expose records when the owning systems publish them.

blocks.title: Troubleshooting
blocks.body: If a lead feels blocked, inspect the item, check related Wiki entries, and confirm required optional modules are loaded before assuming the route is broken.
